claim: Trakt has no outbound webhooks, push notifications, or event stream for third parties; the only 'webhook' in the official API contract is the inbound Plex scrobbler webhook URL (VIP-only). Near-real-time sync must poll /sync/last_activities.
correction: Claim stands as written. Minor precision only: the Plex webhook contract lives under the users contract (GET Plex settings, projects/api/src/contracts/users/index.ts ~L312-317) and exposes webhook.url (VIP-only), last_event_at, event_count, and home_users; the update schema (plexSettingsUpdateSchema.ts) lets the user set only webhook.home_users. No other outbound mechanism exists in the contract. Source: https://github.com/trakt/trakt-api/blob/master/projects/api/src/contracts/users/schema/response/plexSettingsResponseSchema.ts
evidence:
Primary source verified by cloning github.com/trakt/trakt-api at HEAD 832622b63dddc6ef89a4a43c15efae651ed6b911 (committed 2026-11-05) and grepping the full tree, not just the cited file.

1. Only webhook in the API contract is the inbound Plex scrobbler URL, VIP-gated. plexSettingsResponseSchema.ts: webhook.url description reads verbatim "The real-time scrobbler webhook URL; null unless the user is VIP." users/index.ts L315-317 (Get Plex settings): "Returns the authenticated user's Plex connection status, real-time scrobbler webhook info ... `webhook.url` is null unless the user is VIP." Direction is inbound: Plex POSTs to this URL; the schema records last_event_at and event_count of events received.

2. No outbound webhooks, push, or event stream anywhere in the contract. `grep -rli webhook` across the repo hits exactly 5 files: the two Plex settings schemas, users/index.ts, plus two developer-portal files unrelated to the API (confirmPremiumCheckout.ts referencing a Stripe billing webhook, and isSensitiveName.spec.ts containing the string 'webhookSecret' as a test fixture). `grep -rn -iE 'notification|callback_url|event_stream|outbound'` over projects/api/src/contracts/ returns zero hits. Contract directories (calendars, checkin, comments, lists, scrobble, sync, users, etc.) contain no subscription or callback-registration endpoint. `grep -rliE 'websocket|server-sent|text/event-stream|push notification'` hits nothing API-related.

3. last_activities is the documented sync mechanism. projects/api/src/contracts/sync/index.ts L714-719: GET /sync/last_activities, description "Returns the latest activity timestamps for the authenticated user. Cache these dates locally and compare them before syncing to avoid fetching data that has not changed." The caching-and-fresh-data.md guide (updated 2026-07-08) describes only pull patterns ("Use activity and sync endpoints to get IDs and user-specific state").

Secondary corroboration: Pipedream's Trakt "New Show Or Movie Watched" trigger is a polling trigger (https://pipedream.com/apps/trakt/triggers/new-show-or-movie-watched.md); Neowin reports webhook automation is a VIP feature (https://www.neowin.net/amp/trakt-vip-receives-up-to-300-price-hike-going-back-on-promise-to-honor-legacy-subs/). Trakt forum thread https://forums.trakt.tv/t/plex-webhook/19092 now returns "The Trakt Forum is closed"; https://app.trakt.tv/b/plex failed to fetch (header overflow), so the VIP gate rests on the API schema text itself, which is sufficient.

claim: Refresh tokens are single-use: each refresh returns a new refresh_token and invalidates the old one, so the stored pair must be replaced atomically after every refresh. Refresh-token lifetime is undocumented.
correction: Claim is accurate as stated. Minor precision: the guide says the old refresh token is "immediately invalidated" and to "always replace your stored tokens with the values from the response"; it does not use the word "atomically", that is an implementation inference. A useful adjacent fact the guide adds: a failed refresh returns HTTP 400 with {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"session not found"}, and refresh tokens issued before Trakt's auth migration can no longer be exchanged, so the user must re-authorize once. Access tokens are valid for 7 days. No refresh-token lifetime is stated anywhere in the guide, the OAuth contract (projects/api/src/contracts/oauth/index.ts), or the token schemas. Source: https://github.com/trakt/trakt-api/blob/master/projects/developer/src/lib/guides/authentication-oauth.md

(1) The CSV importer is not the only official inbound path: Letterboxd has an official REST API (https://api-docs.letterboxd.com/, access page https://letterboxd.com/api-beta/) with an authenticated write endpoint for creating diary/log entries (client.logEntry.create in the API-mirroring client at https://github.com/Dashron/letterboxd-client). But API access is granted only by emailing an application, and the access page explicitly turns away "private or personal projects", so for a personal Trakt sync it is effectively unavailable. No webhooks exist in the API (only device push-notification registration). (2) The importer has three URLs, not one: watched films/diary at https://letterboxd.com/import/, lists at https://letterboxd.com/list/new/, watchlist at https://letterboxd.com/watchlist/. Also, the import page itself links unofficial third-party "Trakt→Letterboxd" and "Plex→Letterboxd" converters, "maintained by their authors" — so Trakt/Plex paths exist, just not as official integrations. The format limits are confirmed exactly: UTF-8 CSV, "file size limit of 1MB", and "Letterboxd accepts calendar dates for diary entries, not timestamps."

The calendar date on which you watched a title remains constant irrespective of time zone". Import URLs on page: /import/ (watched/diary), /list/new/ (lists), /watchlist/ (watchlist). claim: Letterboxd Terms (October 2026) §6.11 prohibit any robot, spider, scraper or automated tool, and §7 requires access through the provided interface; headless-browser import automation breaches ToS and risks account termination (§21).
correction: Citations are accurate but the claim overstates §6.11 and presents an inference as settled. Verified at https://letterboxd.com/legal/terms-of-use/ ("Last updated: October 2026"): §6.11 reads "Except as explicitly authorized in these Terms, you must not employ any robot, spider, scraper, deep-link, or other automated data gathering or extraction tool, program, or algorithm to access, acquire, copy, or monitor any portion of the Service." It is (a) conditional on explicit authorization elsewhere in the Terms, and (b) scoped to automated data gathering/extraction tools used to access, acquire, copy or monitor the Service, not "any automated tool" without qualification. §7 does say "You agree to access the Service through the interface we provide," and §21 does allow suspension/termination "for any reason or no reason whatsoever, with or without notice," including a material breach. Whether a headless browser driving Letterboxd's own CSV import page breaches §6.11 (which targets gathering/extraction, while importing is submitting data) or §7 (the import page is arguably "the interface we provide") is an interpretation, not stated in the Terms. The termination risk under §21 exists regardless of breach, since it is "for any reason or no reason."
evidence: Fetched https://letterboxd.com/legal/terms-of-use/ directly via curl and reconstructed section numbering from the nested <ol> HTML (numbers are CSS counters, not in the text). Header: "Last updated: October 2026". Item 6.11 verbatim: "Except as explicitly authorized in these Terms, you must not employ any robot, spider, scraper, deep-link, or other automated data gathering or extraction tool, program, or algorithm to access, acquire, copy, or monitor any portion of the Service." Item 7 verbatim start: "No malicious use: You agree to access the Service through the interface we provide. You must not use the Service for any malicious means, interfere with the Service or its security, ..." Item 21 verbatim start: "Termination or suspension of accounts: To the extent permissible by local law, Letterboxd reserves the right to suspend, limit, or terminate your account and your access to the Service for any reason or no reason whatsoever, with or without notice, including if we determine, in our sole discretion, that you have breached any material term of these Terms or as required for urgent security, technical, or legal reason." Section numbers, date, and quoted language all match the claim; the only inaccuracies are the dropped "Except as explicitly authorized" qualifier and the "data gathering or extraction" scope of §6.11, plus the unstated-in-source inference that headless-browser import automation is a breach.

claim: Letterboxd CSV import matches on tmdbID/imdbID and supports WatchedDate, Rating, Rewatch, Tags, Review; 1 MB file size limit.
correction: Claim holds.
